'''Victor Moritz Wagner''' (born 26 April 1997) is a German professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Brooklyn Nets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA).<ref>{{cite web | title=It's Moe Wagner, Not Mo Wagner | first=Giri | last=Nathan | url=https://defector.com/its-moe-wagner-not-mo-wagner | date=December 4, 2024 | website=Defector | publisher=Defector Media LLC | location=New York | access-date=December 4, 2024}}</ref> He played for [[Alba Berlin]]<ref name=":0" /> before moving to the US to play college basketball for the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]] from 2015 through his junior season for the [[2017–18 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2017–18 Wolverines team]]. Wagner entered his name for the [[2017 NBA draft]] without hiring an agent, but withdrew and returned to Michigan. He was selected with the 25th overall pick in the [[2018 NBA draft]] by the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].

He was a 2018 [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] second team selection by both the coaches and the media. Following the season, he was the [[2018 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament]] MVP helping the team earn the Big Ten tournament championship for the second time in a row. He was also named to the West Region All-Tournament Team and Final Four All-Tournament Team during the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2018 NCAA basketball tournament]]. He has represented the [[Germany men's national basketball team|Germany national team]]. His younger brother [[Franz Wagner]] is also an NBA player as well as his former teammate, playing [[small forward]] for the [[Orlando Magic]].

==Early career==
Wagner started his basketball career in the youth ranks of [[Alba Berlin]]. In 2013–14, Wagner played for the club's under-19 Bundesliga squad,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nbbl-basketball.de/teams/nbbl/nordost/#rcd1:/statistik/spieler/index.php%253Fteam_id=1008&pos=&spieler_id=23302&saison=2014|title=Teams der NBBL Nordost|website=NBBL und JBBL|language=de-DE|access-date=March 3, 2016|archive-date=September 8, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170908020322/http://www.nbbl-basketball.de/teams/nbbl/nordost/#rcd1:/statistik/spieler/index.php%253Fteam_id=1008&pos=&spieler_id=23302&saison=2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> which won the German championship.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.basketball-bund.de/news/top4-alba-berlin-kroent-nbbl-meister-139062|title=TOP4: ALBA Berlin krönt sich zum NBBL-Meister – Deutscher Basketball Bund|website=basketball-bund.de|access-date=March 3, 2016|archive-date=June 23, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180623141143/https://www.basketball-bund.de/news/top4-alba-berlin-kroent-nbbl-meister-139062|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2014–15, he played on Alba Berlin's [[Basketball Bundesliga|Bundesliga]] roster, appearing in four games of the German league, scoring 2.3 points per contest.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Moritz Wagner |url=http://www.easycredit-bbl.de/spieler/1657f41c-d4b2-44e5-9c3f-462048a2ef08 |access-date=March 23, 2022 |website=BBL GmbH}}</ref> He also played in two Euroleague games during the 2014–15 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Moritz Wagner |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/players/moritz-wagner/005758/ |access-date=March 23, 2022 |website=euroleaguebasketball.net}}</ref>

==College career==
Wagner first came to the attention of [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|University of Michigan]] head coach [[John Beilein]] in 2014 through an email from a former coaching acquaintance in Germany.<ref name=Anderson>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/22922995/ncaa-tournament-final-four-moe-wagner-michigan-wolverines-career-really-dream-come-true |title=Moe Wagner's Michigan career really is a dream come true |first=Joel |last=Anderson |publisher=ESPN |date=March 27, 2018 |access-date=March 27, 2018}}</ref> Wagner also used social contacts to forward a self-made highlight video to Beilein.<ref name=MMWhtohliNt>{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2018/03/24/michigans-moritz-wagner-having-time-his-life-ncaa-tournament/455003002/|title=Michigan's Moritz Wagner having time of his life in NCAA tournament|access-date=April 4, 2018|date=March 24, 2018|work=[[Detroit Free Press]]|author=Baumgardner, Nick}}</ref> Ultimately, Beilein flew to Berlin to recruit Wagner.<ref name=Anderson/> In April 2015, Wagner announced his decision to attend the University of Michigan and play for the Michigan Wolverines.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/12623456/german-forward-moritz-wagner-commits-michigan-wolverines|title=Wolverines pick up German prospect Wagner|author=Borzello, Jeff|publisher=ESPN|date=April 5, 2015|access-date=March 3, 2016}}</ref> By opting to go to college, he turned down an offer to play professionally.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.berliner-zeitung.de/sport/alba/alba-berlin--der-wechsel-von-albas-talent-moritz-wagner-ist-eine-systemfrage-1132042|title=Alba Berlin : Der Wechsel von Albas Talent Moritz Wagner ist eine Systemfrage|last=Schwager|first=Christian|website=Berliner Zeitung|language=de-DE|access-date=March 3, 2016}}</ref>

===Freshman season===
On March 16, 2016, in the First Four round of the [[2016 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]], Michigan defeated [[2015–16 Tulsa Golden Hurricane men's basketball team|Tulsa]], 67–62. After blocking two shots all season, Wagner posted four [[Block (basketball)|blocks]] and had a season-high eight [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] against Tulsa.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mgoblue.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/031716aaa.html|title=Balanced Attack, Robinson Double-Double Lead U-M Past Tulsa|access-date=March 17, 2016|date=March 16, 2016|website=MGoBlue.com|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160319234215/http://www.mgoblue.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/031716aaa.html|archive-date=March 19, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400871283|title=Zak Irvin leads another late rally as Michigan beats Tulsa|access-date=March 17, 2016|date=March 16, 2016|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref>
[[File:20170301 NW-UM Moe Wagner at the rim.jpg|Wagner in the paint for the [[2016–17 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2016–17 Michigan Wolverines]]|thumb|left]]

===Sophomore season===
Wagner's five [[steal (basketball)|steals]] in the March 9, [[2017 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament]] opener against [[2016–17 Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball team|Illinois]] was a single-game high for the tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/library/stats/mbb-tournament.pdf|title=2017 Big Ten Men's Basketball Tournament Statistics|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170313213648/http://www.bigten.org/library/stats/mbb-tournament.pdf|archive-date=March 13, 2017|access-date=March 13, 2017|date=March 12, 2017|website=BigTen.org|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|url-status=dead}}</ref> Three days later, Michigan won its first Big Ten tournament championship since [[1998 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|1998]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mgoblue.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/031217aaa.html|title=Champions! Michigan Grabs Big Ten tournament Title|access-date=March 12, 2017|date=March 12, 2017|website=MGoBlue.com|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170313125353/http://www.mgoblue.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/031217aaa.html|archive-date=March 13, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> On March 19, Wagner's career-high 26 points helped Michigan defeat [[2016–17 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|Louisville]] 73–69 to advance to the Sweet 16 of the [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400947182|title=Wagner's big game sends Michigan past Louisville in NCAAs|access-date=March 19, 2017|date=March 19, 2017|agency=[[Associated Press]]|publisher=[[ESPN]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mgoblue.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/031917aaa.html|title=How Sweet! U-M Overcomes Louisville, Advances to Round of 16|access-date=March 19, 2017|date=March 19, 2017|website=MGoBlue.com|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170320144751/http://www.mgoblue.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/031917aaa.html|archive-date=March 20, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> For the season, Wagner started all 38 games and averaged 12.1 points and 4.2 rebounds per game, while shooting 39.5% on three-pointers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mlive.com/wolverines/index.ssf/2017/05/moritz_wagner_bypasses_nba_dra.html|title=Moritz Wagner bypasses NBA Draft, will return to Michigan for junior season|access-date=May 24, 2017|date=May 24, 2017|publisher=[[MLive.com]]|author=Quinn, Brendan F.}}</ref> He finished the season as the team's leading rebounder.<ref name=MWrtMDWsid>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/19453883/moe-wagner-returning-michigan-wolverines-dj-wilson-staying-draft|title=Moe Wagner returning to Michigan, D.J. Wilson staying in draft|access-date=May 24, 2017|date=May 24, 2017|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref> Following the season, he was an honorable mention [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] selection by both the coaches and the media.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/big10/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/2016-17/misc_non_event/2016-17_All_Big_Ten_Honors.pdf|title=2016–17 All-Big Ten Men's Basketball Team|access-date=March 7, 2017|date=March 6, 2017|website=BigTen.org|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|archive-date=March 7, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170307123951/http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/big10/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/2016-17/misc_non_event/2016-17_All_Big_Ten_Honors.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mgoblue.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030617aad.html|title=Walton on All-B1G Second Team; Two Earn Honorable Mention|access-date=March 7, 2017|date=March 6, 2017|website=MGoBlue.com|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170307124410/http://www.mgoblue.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030617aad.html|archive-date=March 7, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On April 10, 2017, both Wagner and teammate [[D. J. Wilson]] declared for the [[2017 NBA draft]], but did not hire agents, which gave them until May 24 to withdraw their names and retain their athletic eligibility to return to Michigan.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/19127532/michigan-forwards-moritz-wagner-dj-wilson-declare-nba-draft|title=Moritz Wagner, D.J. Wilson declare for NBA draft, won't hire agents|access-date=April 11, 2017|date=April 10, 2017|author=Goodman, Jeff|publisher=[[ESPN]]}}</ref> Declaring early enabled him to participate in workouts with NBA teams and made him eligible for an invitation to the May 9–14 [[NBA Draft Combine]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mlive.com/wolverines/index.ssf/2017/04/moritz_wagner_nba_pre-write_--.html|title=Moritz Wagner declares for NBA Draft, will test waters without signing with an agent|access-date=April 11, 2017|date=April 10, 2017|website=[[MLive.com]]|author=Quinn, Brendan F.}}</ref> On April 30, 2017, Jeff Goodman of ESPN reported that he was invited to the NBA Draft Combine.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/19273805/nba-invites-more-60-players-draft-combine |title=Sources: Lonzo Ball won't attend draft combine, might be joined by lottery prospects |first=Jeff |last=Goodman |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=April 29, 2017 |access-date=April 30, 2017}}</ref> On May 24, 2017, Wagner decided to pull out of the 2017 draft and return to Michigan for the 2017–18 season.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.maizenbrew.com/basketball/2017/5/24/15685136/moritz-wagner-announces-return-to-michigan-for-2017-18-season|title=Moritz Wagner announces return to Michigan for 2017–18 season|work=Maize n Brew|access-date=May 24, 2017|date=May 24, 2017|author=Broome, Anthony}}</ref>

===Junior season===
[[File:20180206 UM-NW Moe Wagner 7DM26478.jpg|thumb|Wagner for the [[2017–18 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2017–18 Michigan Wolverines]]]]
Wagner was selected to the 2017 10-man preseason All-Big Ten team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/101917aac.html|title=Big Ten Men's Basketball Preseason Honors Announced|access-date=October 27, 2017|date=October 19, 2017|website=BigTen.org|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171022165252/http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/101917aac.html|archive-date=October 22, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was also one of two Big Ten players named to the 21-man [[Karl Malone Award]] watch list.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/102417aaa.html|title=2018 Men's Basketball National Preseason Watch Lists|access-date=October 27, 2017|date=October 24, 2017|website=BigTen.org|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171029034854/http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/102417aaa.html|archive-date=October 29, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was a preseason [[John R. Wooden Award]] and [[Naismith College Player of the Year]] watchlist honoree.<ref name=":8">{{Cite web|url=http://naismithtrophy.com/citizen-naismith-trophy-watch-list-released/|title=Citizen Naismith Trophy Watch List Released|website=naismithtrophy.com|access-date=November 9, 2017|date=November 9, 2017}}</ref><ref name=":9">{{Cite news|url=http://www.woodenaward.com/john_r_wooden_award_presented_by_wendy_s_announces_2017_18_preseason_top_50|title=John R. Wooden Award Presented by Wendy's Announces 2017–18 Preseason Top 50|work=John R Wooden Award|access-date=November 14, 2017|date=November 14, 2017|archive-date=November 15, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171115015543/http://www.woodenaward.com/john_r_wooden_award_presented_by_wendy_s_announces_2017_18_preseason_top_50|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On January 13, 2018, Wagner scored a career-high 27 points as Michigan defeated the fourth-ranked [[2017–18 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State Spartans]] 82–72 in [[East Lansing, Michigan|East Lansing]]; Wagner shot 8-for-13 from the field, including 3-for-4 from three-point range and 8-for-8 from the free-throw line.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.mlive.com/sports/2018/01/michigan_michigan_state_basket.html|title=Moritz Wagner's 27 points lead Michigan to upset win over No. 4 Michigan State|work=MLive.com|access-date=January 13, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=400986504|title=Michigan vs. Michigan State – Box Score |publisher=ESPN|access-date=January 13, 2018|date=January 13, 2018}}</ref> Following the [[2017–18 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|2017–18 Big Ten Conference men's basketball regular season]], Wagner had accumulated more three-point field goals (47) than any NCAA player {{height|ft=6|in=11}} or taller and was a second team All-Big Ten selection by the coaches and the media.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://mgoblue.com/news/2018/2/26/mens-basketball-wagner-robinson-abdur-rahkman-earn-big-ten-honors.aspx|title=Wagner, Robinson and Abdur-Rahkman Earn Big Ten Honors|access-date=February 27, 2018|date=February 26, 2018|website=MGoBlue.com|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|author=Wyrot, Tom}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/022618aad.html|title=Big Ten Unveils Men's Basketball Postseason Honors on BTN|access-date=February 27, 2018|date=February 26, 2018|website=BigTen.org|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180227094314/http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/022618aad.html|archive-date=February 27, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On March 2, Michigan defeated [[2017–18 Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball team|Nebraska]] 77–58 in the quarterfinals of the [[2018 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament]]. Wagner recorded his seventh double-double of the season with 20 points and 13 rebounds. His 13 rebounds marked a single-game high for the 2018 tournament through the first two rounds.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401020037|title=No. 15 Michigan deals blow to Nebraska's NCAA hopes, 77–58|access-date=March 2, 2018|date=March 2, 2018|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://mgoblue.com/news/2018/3/2/mens-basketball-wagners-double-double-guides-michigan-past-nebraska-into-b1g-tournament-semis.aspx|title=Wagner's Double-Double Guides Michigan Past Nebraska, Into B1G Tournament Semis|access-date=March 2, 2018|date=March 2, 2018|website=MGoBlue.com|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|author=Wyrot, Tom}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/030218aag.html|title=Postgame Notes: Michigan-Nebraska|access-date=March 2, 2018|date=March 2, 2018|website=BigTen.org|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180303110209/http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/030218aag.html|archive-date=March 3, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> The following day, in the semifinals of the Big Ten tournament Wagner scored his 1,000th career point, becoming the 54th Wolverine to reach the milestone. He finished the game with a team-high 15 points and eight rebounds in a 75–64 victory over the second-ranked Michigan State Spartans.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401020040|title=Michigan ends top-seeded Spartans' 13-game winning streak|access-date=March 3, 2018|date=March 3, 2018|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://mgoblue.com/news/2018/3/3/mens-basketball-downs-spartans-advances-to-b1g-tournament-final.aspx|title=Wolverines Down Spartans, Advance to B1G Tournament Final|access-date=March 3, 2018|date=March 3, 2018|website=MGoBlue.com|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|author=Wyrot, Tom}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/030318aad.html|title=Postgame Notes: Michigan-Michigan State|access-date=March 3, 2018|date=March 3, 2018|website=BigTen.org|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180304113247/http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/030318aad.html|archive-date=March 4, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> In the March 4, 2018 [[2018 Big Ten men's basketball tournament#Championship|Big Ten tournament championship]] game against [[2017–18 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|Purdue]], Wagner scored 17 points to help lead Michigan to their second consecutive Big Ten tournament championship. Wagner was named the tournament's [[Big Ten tournament Most Outstanding Player|Most Outstanding Player]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401020042|title=Michigan beats Purdue to win 2nd straight Big Ten tournament|access-date=March 4, 2018|date=March 4, 2018|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://mgoblue.com/news/2018/3/4/mens-basketball-back-to-back-wagner-teske-power-michigan-to-second-straight-b1g-tournament-title.aspx|title=Back-to-Back: Wagner, Teske Power Michigan to Second Straight B1G Tournament Title|access-date=March 4, 2018|date=March 4, 2018|website=MGoBlue.com|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|author=Wyrot, Tom}}</ref> In the 2018 tournament, Wagner averaged 15.8 points and 6.5 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180305061946/http://www.bigten.org/library/stats/mbb-tournament.pdf|url=http://www.bigten.org/library/stats/mbb-tournament.pdf|title=2018 Big Ten Men's Basketball Tournament Statistics|access-date=March 5, 2018|archive-date=March 5, 2018|date=March 4, 2018|website=BigTen.org|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]}}</ref>

Wagner, who averaged 12.5 points and 5.5 rebounds in the first four games of the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2018 NCAA basketball tournament]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://mgoblue.com/news/2018/3/26/mens-basketball-two-streaks-collide-wolverines-to-face-ramblers-in-ncaa-semifinal.aspx|title=Two Streaks Collide: Wolverines to Face Ramblers in NCAA Semifinal|access-date=March 29, 2018|date=March 26, 2018|website=MGoBlue.com|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|author=Wyrot, Tom}}</ref> was joined by Wolverines teammates Matthews and [[Muhammad-Ali Abdur-Rahkman]] on the West Region All-tournament team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/marchmadness/status/978070719773986816|title=@MarchMadness status update|publisher=[[NCAA]]|access-date=March 26, 2018|date=March 25, 2018}}</ref>{{Primary source inline|date=November 2023}} Having reached the Final Four, Michigan defeated [[2017–18 Loyola Ramblers men's basketball team|Loyola–Chicago]] 69–57 in the national semifinals on March 31. Wagner recorded his eighth double-double of the season with a game-high 24 points and a career-high 15 rebounds. Wagner became the first player with at least 20 points and 15 rebounds in a national semifinal game since [[Hakeem Olajuwon]] in [[1983 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|1983]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401025887|title=Wagner, Michigan end Loyola's run 69–57 in Final Four|access-date=March 31, 2018|date=March 31, 2018|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://mgoblue.com/news/2018/3/31/mens-basketball-wolverines-take-down-loyola-chicago-to-advance-to-ncaa-championship-game.aspx|title=Wolverines Take Down Loyola Chicago to Advance to NCAA Championship Game|access-date=March 31, 2018|date=March 31, 2018|website=MGoBlue.com|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|author=Wyrot, Tom}}</ref> On April 2, Michigan lost to (#2 [[Coaches Poll]]/#2 [[AP Poll]]) [[2017–18 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova]] 62–79 in the [[2018 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Championship Game|National Championship Game]]. Wagner recorded 16 points and seven rebounds, and was named to the Final Four All-Tournament Team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401025888|title=Villanova takes title, 79–62 over Michigan behind DiVincenzo|access-date=April 3, 2018|date=April 3, 2018|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://mgoblue.com/news/2018/4/2/mens-basketball-michigan-comes-up-short-against-villanova-in-national-championship-game.aspx|title=Michigan Comes Up Short Against Villanova in National Championship Game|access-date=April 3, 2018|date=April 2, 2018|website=MGoBlue.com|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|author=Wyrot, Tom}}</ref> For the tournament he averaged 15.0 points, 7.3 rebounds, 1.3 assists, and 1.2 steals, while shooting 38.5% on his three-point shots.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2767906-march-madness-2018-the-all-tournament-team-after-the-national-championship|title=March Madness 2018: The All-Tournament Team After the National Championship|access-date=April 5, 2018|date=April 3, 2018|publisher=[[Bleacher Report]]|author=Miller, Kerry}}</ref>

For the season, Wagner averaged 14.6 points and 7.1 rebounds and shot 52.8% overall and a team-best 39.4% on his three-point shots.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/2018/04/03/moritz-wagner-charles-matthews-have-decisions-make-nba-draft/33501655/|title=Moritz Wagner, Charles Matthews have decisions to make about NBA Draft|access-date=April 5, 2018|date=April 3, 2018|work=[[Detroit News]]|author=Hawkins, James}}</ref> On March 21, Wagner became an Academic All-Big Ten honoree.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://mgoblue.com/news/2018/3/21/general-winter-academic-all-big-ten-selections-announced.aspx|title=Winter Academic All-Big Ten Selections Announced|access-date=March 29, 2018|date=March 21, 2018|website=MGoBlue.com|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|author=Blevins, Ben}}</ref> On April 14, 2018, Wagner announced that he would enter the 2018 NBA draft and hire an agent.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/23169381/michigan-wolverines-junior-moe-wagner-enters-nba-draft-sign-agent|title=Michigan junior Moe Wagner enters NBA draft, will sign with agent|access-date=April 14, 2018|date=April 14, 2018|publisher=[[ESPN]]|author=Goodman, Jeff}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/michigan-loses-big-man-moe-145459995.html|title=Michigan loses big man Moe Wagner to 2018 NBA draft|access-date=April 14, 2018|date=April 14, 2018|publisher=[[Yahoo! Sports]]|author=Phillips, Scott|archive-date=April 15, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180415060948/https://sports.yahoo.com/michigan-loses-big-man-moe-145459995.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> On May 1, Wagner signed with [[Roc Nation]]'s Joe Branch, who has represented former Michigan teammate [[Caris LeVert]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mlive.com/wolverines/index.ssf/2018/05/former_michigan_basketball_sta_8.html|title=Michigan basketball star Moe Wagner signs with Jay-Z's agency|access-date=May 3, 2018|date=May 1, 2018|website=[[MLive.com]]|author=Kahn, Andrew}}</ref> Later that day, he received an invitation to the [[NBA draft combine]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/2018/05/01/report-matthews-wagner-invited-nba-combine/34439667/|title=Report: Matthews, Wagner invited to NBA Combine|access-date=May 3, 2018|date=May 1, 2018|work=[[Detroit News]]|author=Hawkins, James}}</ref>

news|url=https://www.ocregister.com/2018/06/21/2018-nba-draft-who-is-moritz-wagner-the-lakers-25th-pick/|title=2018 NBA Draft: Who is Moritz Wagner, the Lakers' 25th pick?|date=June 21, ===Washington Wizards (2019–2021)===
[[File:2019 Moe Wagner (48823804703).jpg|thumb|Wagner in 2019]]
On July 6, 2019, Wagner was traded to the [[Washington Wizards]], along with [[Isaac Bonga]], [[Jemerrio Jones]], and a 2022 second-round pick, in a three-team trade where the Lakers acquired [[Anthony Davis]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-acquire-wagner-bonga-jones-lakers-trade|title=Wizards acquire Wagner, Jones and Bonga from Lakers|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=July 5, 2019}}</ref> On November 15, playing against the [[2019–20 Minnesota Timberwolves season|Minnesota Timberwolves]], Wagner became the first NBA player to score 30 points and obtain 15 rebounds coming off the bench since [[Yao Ming]] in 2002 and the first to post such numbers in under 26 minutes played in since [[Len Chappell]] in 1967.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/FredKatz/status/1195546352173932545|title=Moe Wagner is the Man|via=Twitter|author=Katz, Fred|date=November 16, 2019}}</ref>{{Primary source inline|date=November 2023}} Wagner also drew three charges in the game and was the first NBA player to ever post 30 points and 15 rebounds (both career highs) with 4 three-point shots off the bench.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160813 |title=Beal scores 44 again as Wizards beat Timberwolves 137–116 |access-date=November 17, 2019 |date=November 15, 2019 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref> Wagner missed 24 games with an ankle sprain before returning to the lineup on February 3 against the [[2019–20 Golden State Warriors season|Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401161386|title=Alec Burks' 30 points leads Warriors over Wizards 125–117|access-date=February 5, 2020|date=February 3, 2020|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref> He was named to the [[Rising Stars Challenge]] at the [[2020 NBA All-Star Weekend]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/article/2020/01/31/rising-stars-participants-announced-official-release|title=NBA All-Stars Luka Doncic and Trae Young headline U.S. vs. World showdown in 2020 NBA Rising Stars|access-date=February 15, 2020|date=January 31, 2020|publisher=[[National Basketball Association]]}}</ref> where he scored 16 points for the world team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/games/20200214/WLDUSA#/boxscore|title=World 131: Final: USA 151|access-date=February 15, 2020|date=February 14, 2020|publisher=[[National Basketball Association]]}}</ref>

===Boston Celtics (2021)===
On March 25, 2021, Wagner was traded to the [[Boston Celtics]] in a three-team trade involving the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite web|date=March 25, 2021|title=Celtics Acquire Moe Wagner, Luke Kornet in 3-Team Trade|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-acquire-moe-wagner-luke-kornet-3-team-trade|access-date=March 26, 2021|publisher=National Basketball Association}}</ref> On March 26, Wagner made his debut for the Celtics in a 122–114 win over the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], finishing with three points and five rebounds across 10 minutes of play.<ref>{{Cite web|date=March 26, 2021|title=Celtics' Moritz Wagner: Gets 10 minutes in debut|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/celtics-moritz-wagner-gets-10-minutes-in-debut/|access-date=April 18, 2021|website=CBSSports.com|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Terada  |first=Souichi  |date=March 27, 2021 |title=Meet the Celtics' newest big man, Moe Wagner |url=https://www.masslive.com/celtics/2021/03/moe-wagner-trade-meet-the-boston-celtics-newest-big-man-who-already-got-his-feet-wet.html |access-date=April 18, 2021 |website=masslive |language=en}}</ref> On April 16, he was waived by the Celtics.<ref>{{Cite web|date=April 16, 2021|title=Celtics Sign Jabari Parker|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-sign-jabari-parker|access-date=April 18, 2021|publisher=National Basketball Association|quote=In a corresponding roster move, the Celtics have waived center Moe Wagner.}}</ref>

===Orlando Magic (2021–2026)===
Wagner signed with the [[Orlando Magic]] for the rest of the [[2020-21 NBA season]] on April 27, 2021.<ref>{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic Sign Free Agent Center Moritz Wagner|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-sign-moe-wagner-free-agent-center-20210427|website=NBA.com|date=April 27, 2021|access-date=April 28, 2021}}</ref> On April 28, he debuted for the Magic against the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], Wagner scored two points, grabbed two rebounds and dished out an assist across nine minutes in a 109–104 win.<ref>{{cite web|title=Magic's Moritz Wagner: Plays nine minutes in Magic debut|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/magics-moritz-wagner-plays-nine-minutes-in-magic-debut/|website=CBSSports.com|date=April 29, 2021|access-date=May 2, 2021}}</ref> On May 1, he logged a season-high 24 points in his third game with the Magic. Wagner knocked down a 3-pointer that tied the game at 109 with 1 minute and 16 seconds left to play, contributing to the Magic's 112–111 win over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Grizzlies vs. Magic – Game Recap – May 1, 2021 – ESPN|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401307764|website=ESPN.com|access-date=May 2, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Cole Anthony's last-second trey carries Magic past Grizzlies|website=Reuters.com|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/basketball-nba-orl-mem-idUSMTZXEH52GLPICR|date=May 2, 2021|access-date=May 2, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|first=John|last=Denton|title=Anthony's 3-pointer gives Magic 112–111 win over Grizzlies|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/nba/anthonys-3-pointer-gives-magic-112-111-win-over-grizzlies/2021/05/01/0d5838a4-aaf3-11eb-a8a7-5f45ddcdf364_story.html|newspaper=The Washington Post|access-date=May 2, 2021|issn=0190-8286}}</ref> On August 23, he re-signed with Orlando.<ref>{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic Re-Sign Moritz Wagner|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-re-sign-moritz-wagner-20210823|website=NBA.com|date=August 23, 2021|access-date=May 21, 2022}}</ref>

On December 29, 2022, Wagner was suspended by the NBA for two games without pay due to an altercation with [[Detroit Pistons]] guard [[Killian Hayes]] the day before.<ref>{{cite web|title=NBA announces suspensions from Pistons-Magic game|url=https://www.nba.com/news/nba-announces-pistons-magic-suspensions|website=NBA.com|date=December 29, 2022|access-date=December 31, 2022}}</ref>

On July 6, 2023, Wagner signed a two-year, $16 million deal to return to the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic Re-Sign Free Agent Moe Wagner|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/orlando-magic-re-sign-free-agent-moe-wagner-20240706|website=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2024|access-date=July 14, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Magic keep Mo Wagner on 2-year, $16M contract|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/37946029/magic-keep-mo-wagner-2-year-16m-contract|website=ESPN.com|date=July 1, 2023|access-date=February 20, 2024}}</ref> He made 80 appearances (one start) for Orlando during the [[2023–24 NBA season]], averaging 10.9 points, 4.3 rebounds, and 1.2 assists. On July 6, 2024, Wagner re-signed on a two-year, $22 million contract.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 6, 2024 |title=Source: Mo Wagner agrees to new deal with Orlando Magic |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/40483352/mo-wagner-agrees-new-deal-orlando-magic |access-date=2026-05-10 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> In 2024, Wagner's nickname preferences was clarified as "Moe" not "Mo", despite longstanding use of the latter by much of the press.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://defector.com/its-moe-wagner-not-mo-wagner|title=It's Moe Wagner, Not Mo Wagner|accessdate=December 6, 2024|date=December 4, 2024|author=Nathan, Giri|work=[[Defector Media|Defector]]}}</ref>

On December 21, 2024, Wagner suffered a season–ending [[Anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]] tear in left knee while playing against the [[Miami Heat]]. His diagnosis was announced the following day, along with news of an imminent surgery to correct the injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rapp |first=Timothy |title=Magic's Moritz Wagner Reportedly Out for NBA Season After Knee Injury vs. Heat |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10148201-magics-moritz-wagner-reportedly-out-for-nba-season-after-knee-injury-vs-heat |access-date=2024-12-22 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}}</ref> Wagner had once again operated as a back up prior to his injury, averaging 12.9 points, 4.9 rebounds, and 1.4 assists over 30 appearances (one start).

On July 4, 2025, Wagner re-signed with the Magic on a one-year, $5 million contract.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Charania |first=Shams  |author-link=Shams Charania |date=July 4, 2025 |title=Sources: Moe Wagner returns to Magic on 1-year, $5M deal |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/45668460/sources-moe-wagner-returns-magic-1-year-5m-deal |access-date=September 17, 2025 |website=espn.com |language=en}}</ref> On January 11, 2026, Wagner made his first appearance since the ACL injury, recording eight points in 10 minutes played during a 128–118 victory over the [[2025–26 New Orleans Pelicans season|New Orleans Pelicans]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Magic's Moritz Wager returns ahead of road trip to Germany|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/47585625/magic-moritz-wagner-returns-ahead-road-trip-germany|access-date=January 16, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref>

==National team career==
===Junior national team===
Wagner won gold with the Germany U18 national team at the [[2014 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship Division B]] in Bulgaria.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/history/261-fiba-u18-eurobasket-division-b/7866/players/210175-moritz-wagner|title=Moritz Wagner FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship Division B statistics|website=FIBA.basketball|access-date=March 3, 2016}}</ref> Averaging 16.1 points per contest, Wagner was Germany's leading scorer at the [[2017 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/history/281-fiba-u20-eurobasket/10364/players/210175-moritz-wagner|title=Moritz Wagner FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship statistics|website=FIBA.basketball|access-date=August 2, 2017}}</ref>

===Senior national team===
Wagner helped Germany qualify for the [[Basketball at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2020 Summer Olympics]], where he earned the MVP award in the [[2020 FIBA Men's Olympic Qualifying Tournaments – Split|Olympic qualifying tournament]] in Split, Croatia.<ref>{{cite news |title=A point per minute: Moritz Wagner picks up the TISSOT MVP award in Split |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/news/oqt-croatia-2020-news-a-point-per-minute-moritz-wagner-picks-up-the-tissot-mvp-award-in-split |work=FIBA.basketball |access-date=July 4, 2021}}</ref> During the event in Tokyo, he averaged 11 points per game.<ref>{{cite news |title=Moritz Wagner at the Tokyo 2020 Men's Olympic Basketball Tournament |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/history/320-mens-olympic-basketball-tournament/9562/players/210175-moritz-wagner |work=FIBA.basketball |access-date=August 5, 2021}}</ref> A few years later, in September 2023, Wagner helped Germany win their first world title at the [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup|2023 FIBA World Cup]]. He finished with averages of 11.9 points and 4.8 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite news|title=Moritz Wagner at the 2023 FIBA World Cup|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/history/201-fiba-basketball-world-cup/208182/players/210175-moritz-wagner|work=FIBA.basketball|access-date=September 10, 2023}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Wagner has a younger brother, [[Franz Wagner|Franz]], who is his former teammate on the [[Orlando Magic]] and played basketball for [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/franz-wagner/20391|title=Franz Wagner – Men's Basketball|website=University of Michigan Athletics|language=en|access-date=December 1, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Zuke |first1=Ryan |title=Franz Wagner becomes Michigan basketball's first top-10 pick since 2014, drafted by Orlando Magic |url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/2021/07/franz-wagner-becomes-michigan-basketballs-first-top-10-pick-since-2014-drafted-by-orlando-magic.html |access-date=July 30, 2021 |work=[[MLive.com]] |date=July 29, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/orlando-magic-sign-jalen-suggs-franz-wagner-nba-draft-contract-20210803|title=Orlando Magic Sign Jalen Suggs and Franz Wagner|accessdate=May 21, 2022|date=August 3, 2021|publisher=[[National Basketball Association]]}}</ref>

Wagner is a fan of the [[Bundesliga]] football club [[SV Werder Bremen|Werder Bremen]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-08-08 |title=Basketball-Star Moritz Wagner ist sein "gesamtes Leben Werder-Bremen-Fan" – trotz des Spottes von Bruder Franz |url=https://www.deichstube.de/news/werder-bremen-fan-moritz-wagner-basketball-star-gruende-olympia-bruder-franz-wagner-spott-lustig-orlando-magic-dbb-deutschland-zr-93210301.html |access-date=2025-02-21 |website=www.deichstube.de |language=de}}</ref>
